cases.issue_title: [bug]: fully cancelling a paid seated booking refunds only one seat's payment
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

On a seated paid event, every attendee booking the same time slot creates a separate `Payment` record, but all of those payments belong to the same booking. When the host fully cancels that booking and the event's **Refund on cancellation** policy is set to **Always** or **Days**, only one attendee is refunded. The remaining attendees have their bookings cancelled but their successful payments are never refunded, and no error is reported.

The refund flow currently resolves only the first successful payment for a booking. Although the cancellation flow passes all booking payments into the refund handler, `processPaymentRefund.ts` selects a single payment via `payment.find((p) => p.success)` and issues only one refund request, silently ignoring the rest.

This is different from **#29664**, which affected the booking confirmation page UI. This issue causes real payment refunds to be skipped.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a paid event type with:

   * `seatsPerTimeSlot > 1`
   * a payment provider (e.g. Stripe) connected
   * **Refund on cancellation** set to **Always** (or **Days**).
2. Have two (or more) different attendees book and successfully pay for the same time slot.
3. As the host, cancel the entire booking (not removing an individual seat/attendee).
4. Check the payment provider (e.g. Stripe) dashboard for refunds.

---

### Actual Results

* Only the first successful payment associated with the booking is refunded.
* The remaining successful payments are left untouched.
* The booking is cancelled for every attendee, but the other attendees remain charged.
* No error or warning is surfaced.

---

### Expected Results

* Every successful payment associated with the cancelled booking should be refunded, subject to the configured refund policy (Always/Days and any applicable cutoff).
* If multiple attendees paid for the same booking, each successful payment should receive its own refund.

---

### Technical details

* **Type:** Backend payment/refund logic bug.
* **Reproduces on:** Current `main`.
* **Browser / Node.js:** Not browser-dependent (backend issue).
* **Affected code:**

  * `packages/features/bookings/lib/payment/processPaymentRefund.ts`

    * Uses `payment.find((p) => p.success)`, refunding only the first successful payment.
  * `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`

    * Correctly passes all booking payments (`payment: true`) into the refund flow, but only one is ultimately processed.
* **Impact:** Occurs only when:

  * the event has multiple seats,
  * multiple attendees have paid,
  * and the event uses automatic refunds on cancellation.

---

### Evidence

The issue was reproduced with automated tests.

* **Unit test (`processPaymentRefund.test.ts`)**

  * Created a booking containing two successful payments.
  * Expected `handlePaymentRefund` to be called once per successful payment.
  * On current `main`, only one refund is issued, confirming the bug.
  * After changing the implementation to refund every successful payment, the test passes.

* **Integration test (`handleCancelBooking.test.ts`)**

  * Cancelled a seated booking with multiple successful payments.
  * Verified that `handleCancelBooking` correctly passes all payments into `processPaymentRefund`.
  * Confirms the loss occurs inside `processPaymentRefund`, where only the first successful payment is selected for refund.

cases.issue_title: Test push notification opens https://app.cal.com instead of the self-hosted Cal.diy instance
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

When a user enables push notifications, the server immediately sends a "Test Notification". The notification payload hardcodes `url: "https://app.cal.com/"`. The service worker uses exactly that `data.url` to navigate when the notification is clicked (`self.clients.openWindow(url)`), so on any self-hosted Cal.diy instance the test notification sends the user to **cal.com**, not their own deployment. Cal.diy is self-host-only, so this is wrong for the entire intended audience.

Every other place in the codebase that needs the app URL uses `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL || "https://app.cal.com"` (see `CalendarEventBuilder.ts`, `getPublicEvent.ts`, `RegularBookingService.ts`, etc.)  this handler is the only one that hardcodes the URL with no env fallback.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Self-host Cal.diy with `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL` set to your own domain.
2. Sign in, go to settings, and enable push notifications.
3. Receive the "Test Notification" and click it.

### Actual Results

- The notification opens `https://app.cal.com/` (the public Cal.com app), not the user's own instance.

### Expected Results

- The notification should open the configured instance URL, e.g. `WEBAPP_URL` from `@calcom/lib/constants` (or `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL`).

### Technical details

- The hardcoded URL: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L68
- The service worker consumes `data.url` here: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/apps/web/public/service-worker.js#L86-L94
- While in this file, two adjacent robustness/i18n nits are worth fixing in the same PR:
  - `JSON.parse(subscription)` at https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L32 is not wrapped in try/catch — malformed JSON throws an uncaught error and returns a 500 instead of a clean `BAD_REQUEST`.
  - The notification `title`/`body` (lines 66–67) are hardcoded English and aren't localized to the user's locale.

### Evidence

https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L60-L74

cases.issue_title: Calendar subscription sync ignores Cal.diy iCalUIDs
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

Calendar subscription sync currently filters incoming calendar events by checking whether the event `iCalUID` ends with `@cal.com`.

However, Cal.diy generates booking iCalUIDs using the configured app name. In a default Cal.diy setup, `APP_NAME` defaults to `Cal.diy`, so generated booking UIDs can look like:

`test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`

Because the sync filter only accepts `@cal.com`, valid Cal.diy booking events can be skipped during calendar subscription sync. This means changes made from a connected calendar, such as cancelling or moving a synced booking event, may not be processed for default/self-hosted Cal.diy bookings.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a default Cal.diy setup where `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` is not overridden.
2. Create a booking that gets an iCalUID using the default app name, for example `test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`.
3. Pass a calendar subscription event with that iCalUID into `CalendarSyncService.handleEvents`.
4. Observe that the event is filtered out before cancellation or reschedule handling runs.

### Actual Results

- Calendar subscription sync only processes events whose `iCalUID` ends with `@cal.com`.
- Valid Cal.diy iCalUIDs such as `test-booking-uid@Cal.diy` are ignored.
- The booking repository is never queried for the booking UID.
- Calendar-side changes may not sync back into Cal.diy.

### Expected Results

- Calendar subscription sync should process Cal-managed booking events generated by Cal.diy.
- UIDs ending in the default Cal.diy suffix should be accepted.
- Legacy `@cal.com` UIDs should continue to work.
- External calendar UIDs such as `@google.com` or `@external.com` should still be ignored.

### Technical details

- `APP_NAME` defaults to `Cal.diy` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`.
- iCalUID generation uses `APP_NAME` in `packages/emails/lib/getICalUID.ts`.
- Calendar subscription sync currently filters only `@cal.com` in `packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/sync/CalendarSyncService.ts`.

### Evidence

I reproduced this with a focused unit test around `CalendarSyncService.handleEvents`.

A regression test using:

`test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`

fails with the current `@cal.com`-only filter because the event is not processed.

After updating the filter to accept Cal-managed iCalUID suffixes, the targeted calendar sync test passes:

`yarn vitest run packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/sync/__tests__/CalendarSyncService.test.ts`

Result:

`21 tests passed`

cases.issue_title: Add-on (priced booking field) charges are dropped for additional seat bookers on paid seated events
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

On a paid event that has both `seatsPerTimeSlot` set **and** priced booking fields (e.g. a `number` "tickets" field, or a priced `select`/`checkbox`/`boolean`/`radio` option), only the **first** booker for a slot is charged for their add-ons. Every **subsequent** seat booker is charged the **base price only** — their add-on selections are silently dropped from the payment, so the organizer loses that revenue on every seat after the first.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a paid event type (e.g. Stripe, base price $10) with `seatsPerTimeSlot: 3`.
2. Add a priced booking field — e.g. a `number` field named "tickets" at $5 each.
3. **Booker A** (first seat) books and selects `tickets = 3` → charged $10 + 3×$5 = **$25** (correct).
4. **Booker B** (second seat, joining the same slot) selects `tickets = 3`.

Why it's a bug: the first booker for a slot falls back to the regular booking path, which charges add-ons; subsequent seat bookings go through a different path that does not.

### Actual Results

* Booker B is charged **$10** (base price only); their `tickets = 3` add-on ($15) is never added to the payment.
* The organizer loses the add-on revenue for every seat after the first.

### Expected Results

* Every seat booker is charged the base price plus their selected add-ons, exactly like the first booker (Booker B should be charged **$25**).

### Technical Details

* The first seat falls back to `RegularBookingService`, which passes `bookingFields` to `handlePayment` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:2308`).
* Subsequent seats route through `createNewSeat`, whose `handlePayment(...)` call **omits `bookingFields`** (and `locale`) (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/create/createNewSeat.ts:262`).
* In `handlePayment`, the add-on pricing loop is gated by `if ((bookingFields || []).length > 0)` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handlePayment.ts:81`), so when `bookingFields` is undefined, the add-ons are never computed and `totalAmount` remains at the base price.
* Not browser-specific; this is backend booking/payment logic.

### Evidence

* Verified by tracing the two `handlePayment` call sites. Only `RegularBookingService` passes `bookingFields`; `createNewSeat` does not. Also confirmed the add-on gate in `handlePayment`.
* Covered by a new unit test asserting that `createNewSeat` forwards `bookingFields` to `handlePayment`. The test **fails** on current `main` (called without `bookingFields`) and **passes** with the fix.
* A PR containing the fix and test is ready.

cases.issue_title: fix: Security and code quality issues in tRPC routers
cases.issue_body:
## Bug: Security and code quality issues in tRPC routers

### Description

Multiple security and code quality issues found across tRPC routers in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/`:

### 1. 🔴 `credential.key` exposed via `credentials: true` in Prisma query

**File**: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/util.ts` (line 42)

The booking middleware uses `credentials: true` in a Prisma `include`, which fetches **all** credential fields including the sensitive `key` field containing OAuth tokens and API secrets. Per project rules: *"Never expose `credential.key` field in API responses or queries"*.

```typescript
// BEFORE (vulnerable): fetches ALL fields including credential.key
credentials: true,
```

### 2. 🔴 `console.log` leaking private hashed link data in production

**File**: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/update.handler.ts` (lines 611, 615)

Two `console.log` statements dump private hashed link data to stdout in production:

```typescript
console.log("multiplePrivateLinks", multiplePrivateLinks);
console.log("connectedLinks", connectedLinks);
```

### 3. 🔴 `console.log(e)` instead of structured logger

**File**: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/availability/schedule/getScheduleByEventTypeSlug.handler.ts` (line 60)

Error details leaked via raw `console.log` instead of the project's structured `logger`.

### 4. 🟡 Prisma `include` instead of `select` (performance)

**Files**:
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/getEventTypesFromGroup.handler.ts` (line 179) — membership query fetches all columns
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/duplicate.handler.ts` (lines 41-43) — `hosts: true`, `team: true`, `webhooks: true` fetch all columns

### 5. 🟡 `@ts-expect-error` hiding type-safety issues

**File**: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/update.handler.ts` (line 729)

`@ts-expect-error` used to suppress implicit any type on a reduce — can be fixed with proper `Record<string, unknown>` typing.

### Expected behavior

- Credential queries should only `select` non-sensitive fields (`id`, `type`, `appId`)
- No `console.log` in production code; use structured `logger`
- Prisma queries should use `select` instead of `include` per project rules
- No `@ts-expect-error` when proper typing is feasible

### Area
- area: bookings, event-types, availability

cases.issue_title: scroll doesn't load more users, no loaded count indicator, missing spacing
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

The admin users table at `/settings/admin/users` has three UX problems:

1. **Infinite scroll does not load more users** — scrolling to the bottom of the table container does not trigger fetching the next page of users. The scroll event was attached to a fixed-height `div` but the `onScroll` handler was passing the wrong element reference (`tableContainerRef.current` evaluated at call time instead of `e.currentTarget`), so the trigger never fired.

2. **No indication of how many users are loaded** — there is no counter or text showing the user how many results are currently loaded vs. the total (e.g. "Showing 25 of 43"). Users have no feedback about whether more data exists.

3. **No margin/spacing between the search bar and the table** — the search input sits flush against the table border with no gap, making the layout feel cramped and hard to read.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Go to `/settings/admin/users` as an admin
2. Observe that the table loads the first 25 users
3. Scroll to the bottom of the table container
4. **Expected**: next page of users loads automatically
5. **Actual**: nothing happens, no more users are loaded
6. Also observe: no text showing "Showing 25 of 43" or similar
7. Also observe: search bar and table are visually merged with no spacing

### Actual Results

- Scrolling to the bottom of the users table does not fetch the next page
- There is no count indicator (e.g. "Showing X of Y users")
- No spacing between the search bar and the table border
- No "Load more" button as a fallback

### Expected Results

- Scrolling near the bottom of the table container triggers loading the next page automatically
- A "Showing X of Y" counter is visible above the table, updating as more pages load
- An inline loading row appears inside the table while the next page is fetching
- A "Load more" button is rendered below the table as an explicit fallback
- A "No more results" message appears when all users have been loaded
- Proper spacing (`gap-4`) between the search bar and the table

cases.issue_title: Update Password button is enabled when the password form is invalid
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

The **Update Password** button in Settings → Security becomes enabled as soon as the form is modified, even when required fields are empty or validation requirements are not satisfied.

The button state is currently tied to `isDirty` rather than the overall validity of the form, resulting in an inconsistent user experience where users can attempt to submit invalid password data.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to **Settings → Security**.
2. Modify one of the password fields.
3. Leave one or more required fields empty, or enter a password that does not satisfy the password requirements.
4. Observe the state of the **Update Password** button.

### Actual Results

* The **Update Password** button becomes enabled once the form is modified, even when the form is invalid.

### Expected Results

* The **Update Password** button should only be enabled when:

  * All required fields are filled.
  * Password validation requirements are satisfied.
  * The form has been modified.

cases.issue_title: Filtering on Boolean columns has a limitation in Snowflake (and possibly other databases)
cases.issue_body:
### Bug description

In chart creator, I can't apply a filter on a Boolean column (e.g. to just return rows where the column is `True`) when using Snowflake.

The generated Snowflake SQL isn't valid, because `IS True` isn't valid in Snowflake. This is the generated SQL:

```
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "count" 
FROM flights.fct_flight_stats 
WHERE "IS_CANCELLED" IS true
 LIMIT 5000
```

`IS` can only be used to evaluate NULL-ness in Snowflake, not for filtering values (read more [here](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constructs/where#usage-notes) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76759093/how-to-query-with-filter-boolean-column-with-is-in-snowflake)). I suspect this is also true for some other databases, but I haven't researched thoroughly. 

The alternative would be to have menu options for `= True` and `= False`, for Boolean columns.

**Version**

Preset Cloud // Apache Superset 4.2.0.5

**Workarounds**

1. The `IN` option can be used in combination with and limiting the values to `True`.  
- However, if the generated SQL errored previously, the IN option mysteriously disappears in the UI for this Boolean column. I suspect this is because Superset isn't aware of valid values to fetch that would work for `IN`. I'm happy to open a separate issue for this if the community would like!

2. Use the Custom SQL tab and manually specify `= True`.

cases.issue_title: HOURS OFFSET applies only to 1 time column, it should apply to all temporal columns in the dataset
cases.issue_body:
In Dataset Settings there is an option called "HOURS OFFSET". 
When you have only one time column, it's working as expected: it adds the corresponding number of hours to the time column while outputting it on the chart. However, when you have more than one temporal columns, the number of hours is logically expected to be added to all of them. Now it adds to only the one column that is selected as the "TIME COLUMN" in the chart.

#### How to reproduce the bug

1. Create a dataset with more than one temporal field (e.g. Creation and expiration dates, as in the screencast),
2. Add "HOURS OFFSET" to the dataset settings (e.g. 4) and save the dataset,
3. Choose a "TIME COLUMN" in the Time settings of the chart and click Update,
4. Choose another "TIME COLUMN" and click Update

### Expected results
X hours (set in "HOURS OFFSET") should be added to all temporal fields, regardless of the "TIME COLUMN" selected.

### Actual results
X hours are added to only one column, the one that is selected as the "TIME COLUMN" in the chart.

Note, that in the screencast, the "Expire Date" of the bottom row is actually equal to the "Agreement Creation Date" of the top row, but they are displayed with a 4-hour difference either way, because of the "HOURS OFFSET" option set.

cases.issue_title: [Bug]: Selective library scan fails with `invalid argument` on `rofs-filtered` FUSE mount
cases.issue_body:
### I confirm that:

- [x] I have searched the existing [open AND closed issues](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/issues?q=is%3Aissue) to see if an issue already exists for the bug I've encountered
- [x] I'm using the latest version (your issue may have been fixed already)

### Version

0.63.2

### Current Behavior

Hello there,

I ran into a problem with the selective scan functionality and wanted to report it in case this is a bug or an incompatibility with FUSE filesystems.

I am running **Navidrome 0.63.2 (`be10f89c`) in Docker on DietPi**.

I have three libraries:

```text
1 | Music Library | /music
2 | Collection    | /jukebox/collection
3 | Essentials    | /jukebox/essentials
```

`/music` is a normal bind mount. The other two libraries are directories provided through `rofs-filtered` FUSE mounts.

The interesting part is that everything works fine when I use Navidrome normally. In particular, starting a library scan from the web interface works, and a normal full scan from the CLI also works:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full
```

This successfully scans all three libraries, including the two FUSE-based ones.

The problem only seems to occur when I try to scan a specific library using the CLI `--target` option.

For example:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full --target "2:/jukebox/collection"
```

Navidrome reports:

```text
Scanning specific folders
Scanner: Starting selective scan fullScan=true numLibraries=1 numTargets=1
Scanner: Target folder does not exist.
error="open /jukebox/collection: invalid argument"
path=/jukebox/collection
```

The same happens without `--full`:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan \
  --target "2:/jukebox/collection"
```

and also with the `Essentials` library:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full \
  --target "3:/jukebox/essentials"
```

What confuses me is that the directory definitely exists and is accessible from inside the container.

For example:

```bash
docker exec navidrome ls -la /jukebox/collection
```

returns:

```text
_Archive
_Collection
_Kids
```

And:

```bash
docker exec navidrome sh -c 'cd /jukebox/collection && pwd && find . -maxdepth 1 -type d -print'
```

also works:

```text
/jukebox/collection
.
./_Kids
./_Collection
./_Archive
```

Even `stat` and `test -d` work correctly.

The relevant Docker mounts are:

```text
bind /mnt/volume1/shared/jukebox -> /music
bind /mnt/volume1/shared/.navidrome/data -> /data
bind /mnt/fuse_mnt/jukebox -> /jukebox
```

On the host, the two affected directories are mounted using `rofs-filtered`:

```text
rofs-filtered on /mnt/fuse_mnt/jukebox/collection type fuse.rofs-filtered
rofs-filtered on /mnt/fuse_mnt/jukebox/essentials type fuse.rofs-filtered
```

I also tried targeting a subdirectory:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full --target "2:/jukebox/collection/_Collection"
```

but this gives the same `invalid argument` error.

So at the moment my workaround is simply to run:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full
```

which works perfectly, but of course scans all libraries.

I am wondering if there is some difference in how the selective scanner opens/resolves the `--target` path compared to the normal scanner, and whether this could be related to the `rofs-filtered` FUSE filesystem.

If anyone has an idea what might cause this, or if there is anything else I could test to help track it down, I'd be happy to provide more information.

Thanks!

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the `--target` option to scan the specified library/folder successfully, just like a normal full scan does.

Since the folder exists and is accessible from inside the container, I would expect:

```bash
docker exec navidrome /app/navidrome scan --full --target "2:/jukebox/collection"
```

cases.issue_title: DAP: 'invalid type: map, expected unit' on configurationDone response when adapter returns body={}
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

`vscode-js-debug` (the DAP adapter Helix's `js-debug-dap` block is wired for) returns `body: {}` on the `configurationDone` response. Helix declares `ConfigurationDone::Result = ()` (unit type), so `serde_json::from_value::<()>(Value::Object({}))` fails with:

```
Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit
```

The error is shown to the user via `Editor::set_error` in the `Initialized` event handler, but the debug session continues (`set_active_client` runs regardless). The adapter has already accepted the request and returned `success: true`, so the debugger is actually running — the error is misleading, not fatal.

### Reproduction Steps

**`~/.config/helix/languages.toml`**

```toml
[[language]]
name = "javascript"

[language.debugger]
name = "js-debug-dap"
transport = "tcp"
port-arg = "{} 127.0.0.1"
command = "node"
args = ["/path/to/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js"]
quirks = { absolute-paths = true }

[[language.debugger.templates]]
name = "source"
request = "launch"
completion = [{ name = "main", completion = "filename", default = "index.js" }]
args = { type = "pwa-node", program = "{0}", skipFiles = ["<node_internals>/**"] }
```

**Adapter install** (Microsoft's prebuilt `js-debug-dap` release tarball, not the VS Code extension):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/lib/js-debug && cd ~/lib/js-debug
curl -L -o js-debug-dap.tar.gz \
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-js-debug/releases/download/v1.117.0/js-debug-dap-v1.117.0.tar.gz
tar -xzf js-debug-dap.tar.gz && rm js-debug-dap.tar.gz
# Entry point: ~/lib/js-debug/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js
```

**Steps:**

1. `echo 'console.log("hello")' > /tmp/index.js`
2. `hx /tmp/index.js`
3. Set a breakpoint (`<space>gb` on line 1)
4. `:debug-start source<ret>index.js<ret>`

**Expected:** debug session starts, status bar shows "Debugged application started".

**Actual:** status bar shows `Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit`. The debuggee actually starts, but the error message implies failure.

## Captured raw DAP response

Verified against the adapter directly (no Helix in the loop):

```json
{"seq": 2, "type": "response", "request_seq": 3, "command": "configurationDone", "success": true, "body": {}}
```

vscode-js-debug returns `body: {}` on every `configurationDone` response. This is technically non-DAP-compliant — the spec for `configurationDone`'s response has no body — but the same `{}` body shape is used by many other adapters (JDTLS, etc.) and Helix handles it elsewhere via `serde_json::Value` result types.


### Helix log

<details><summary>~/.cache/helix/helix.log</summary>

```
helix_dap::transport [INFO] -> DAP {"type":"request","seq":3,"command":"configurationDone","arguments":{}}
helix_dap::transport [INFO] <- DAP {"seq":4,"type":"response","request_seq":3,"command":"configurationDone","success":true,"body":{}}
helix_dap::transport [INFO] <- DAP success in response to 3
helix_view::editor [ERROR] editor error: Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit
```

</details>

cases.issue_title: Highlighting of inline math equations in markdown
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

Certain flavors of markdown support inline equations written in latex syntax, e.g. `some text $E=mc^2$ more text`. While the markdown tree-sitter used by helix supports the injection of latex, it appears the dollar-sign delimiters are not passed along to the latex tree-sitter. In the example, this means the latex tree-sitter has no way to know that `E=mc^2` is an equation and should be highlighted accordingly. Instead, it is highlighted as ordinary text, which is easy to verify with a minimal `.tex` file.

Fixing the issue is as easy as replacing the last occurrence (and only the last occurrence) of `injection.include-unnamed-children` with `injection.include-children` in the file `runtime/queries/markdown.inline/injections.scm` since this will cause the dollar-sign delimiters to be passed to the latex tree-sitter. At least, this fixed the problem for me.

**NB** Since `include-unnamed-children` is a helix extension of tree-sitter, this is a bug with helix and not a bug with tree-sitter.

### Reproduction Steps

Run the commands below then open `test.md` and `test.tex` in helix to compare syntax highlighting. Make sure to apply a theme that uses a special color for `@markup.raw` since that is the scope applied to latex equations.

```bash
echo 'some text $E=mc^2$ more text' > test.md
cat > test.tex << 'EOF'
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}

E=mc^2 (this is how equations appear in markdown files)

$E=mc^2$ (this is how equations should appear in markdown files)

\end{document}
EOF
```

### Summary

Weird theme resets on termina::Csi::Mode::ReportTheme event captures. Or maybe the Csi event being triggered there is in itself weird, Im not familiar enough with terminal control sequences to be able to tell. 

### Reproduction Steps

<!-- Ideally provide a key sequence and/or asciinema.org recording. --> 

I tried this:

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/T89qgsB5xlOMmVzO.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/T89qgsB5xlOMmVzO)

It's not very clear in the recording but I pressed `ctrl+` 2 times, which enlarges the terminal font size twice. 
Opening or closing a new terminal window in the same workspace (hyprland) also seems to sometimes trigger this.

I expected this to happen:
Nothing happens, the theme I set earlier with `:theme <name>` is respected as the current theme.

Instead, this happened:
The current theme is overwritten with the theme set in the config.toml file.

the offending code is here: https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/3beb268068d23294a26b47eab43b0a13a2a3a951/helix-term/src/application.rs#L725-L732

Calling Self::load_configured_theme resets the theme back to the configuration file theme. Commenting out this function call fixes the problem, although, Im not sure if it doesnt break something else, or why this behavior may be desired over reloading the current editor theme. 



### Helix log

None, the log doesn't contain anything useful to this.

Linux

foot version: 1.26.1 +pgo +ime +graphemes +toplevel-tag +blur -assertions

source

### Bug description

App-passwords (auth tokens) created through:

`sudo -u www-data php occ user:auth-tokens:add <user>`

are invalidated 5 minutes (with a few seconds difference every time) after creation. During the first 5 minutes they work perfectly for WebDAV and OCS API calls.

After ~300 seconds the next request fails with response status code 503 and:

```
Session token credentials are invalid
OC\Authentication\Exceptions\TokenPasswordExpiredException
```
and in the database the token’s `password_invalid` field flips from `0` → `1`.

This happens both for normal local users and SAML users.

I have tried to disable external IdP, password-policy, and all background-jobs, but no I have had no difference.

1. Create a new permanent token using the user password when prompted for a password:
 `sudo -u www-data php occ user:auth-tokens:add <username>`
2. Output: App password: `<app-password>`
3. Test the password immediately: `curl -u <username>:<token> https://nextcloud-poc.dc.kau.se/remote.php/dav/files/<username>/ -I` 
  → Response status `200`
4. Wait 5+ minutes.
5. Repeat the same request.
 → Response status `503 Service unavailable`, and then `401 Unauthorized` on the next one.
6. Check database:
`SELECT id,name,type,last_activity,password_invalid FROM oc_authtoken ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3;`
The token row now has `password_invalid = 1`.




### Expected behavior

Permanent app tokens (type 1) should remain valid indefinitely unless explicitly revoked or the user password changes. They should not **expire after 5 minutes** nor set `password_invalid = 1`.

Actual behavior:
App tokens created via occ user:auth-tokens:add are invalidated after 5 minutes of inactivity, throwing TokenPasswordExpiredException on next use after 5 minutes.

cases.issue_title: Chunked uploading - `MOVE` with `Content-Length: 0` results in 0bytes files in Object Storage
cases.issue_body:
> A related finding on this same code path, with a second trigger that does **not** involve chunked transfer encoding — and which `fastcgi_request_buffering on` does *not* fix.
> 
> **Symptom:** uploading a large file through the web UI in Safari (26.6, macOS) stores a 0-byte file. Every request reports success — `MKCOL` 201, all five chunk `PUT`s 201, assembly `MOVE .../.file` 201 — and nothing is logged. The same file in Chrome uploads correctly. Server: 33.0.7, nginx + php-fpm, S3 (MinIO) primary storage, `fastcgi_request_buffering on`.
> 
> **Cause:** on the assembly step, `File::put()` takes the expected write size from the *MOVE request's own* `Content-Length` — a header that describes the MOVE (which carries no body), not the assembled stream being written:
> 
> `apps/dav/lib/Connector/Sabre/File.php` (33.0.7, lines 209-223)
> ```php
> $lengthHeader = $this->request->getHeader('content-length');
> $expected = $lengthHeader !== '' ? (int)$lengthHeader : null;
> ...
> $count = $partStorage->writeStream($internalPartPath, $wrappedData, $expected);
> ```
> 
> Safari sends `Content-Length: 0` on the MOVE. Chrome omits the header entirely. Since `"0" !== ''`, Safari yields `$expected = 0` while Chrome yields `null`. That matters because `ObjectStoreStorage::writeStream()` only determines the real size when it was not given one:
> 
> `lib/private/Files/ObjectStore/ObjectStoreStorage.php`
> ```php
> public function writeStream(string $path, $stream, ?int $size = null): int {
>     if ($size === null) {
>         $stats = fstat($stream);
>         if (is_array($stats) && isset($stats['size'])) {
>             $size = $stats['size'];
>         }
>     }
> ```
> 
> So Safari's `0` skips the `fstat()` fallback and 0 bytes are written, reported as 201. Chrome's `null` runs the fallback and gets the correct length.
> 
> This appears to be **specific to object-storage primary storage**: `OC\Files\Storage\Local::writeStream()` ignores the `$size` argument altogether and just does `file_put_contents()`, so a local-storage install should not be affected.
> 
> **Reproduction** with plain curl — no browser involved. 102395904-byte file, five chunks (4×20971520 + 18509824), `fastcgi_request_buffering on` throughout. The single variable is the `Content-Length` header on the MOVE:
> 
> | chunk PUTs | `Content-Length: 0` on MOVE | result |
> |---|---|---|
> | sequential | no | 102395904 bytes — correct |
> | sequential | **yes** | **0 bytes**, MOVE 201 |
> | parallel | no | 102395904 bytes — correct |
> | parallel | **yes** | **0 bytes**, MOVE 201 |
> 
> ```bash
> ID=repro
> curl -X MKCOL "$BASE/remote.php/dav/uploads/$USER/$ID"
> n=1; for p in part.*; do curl -X PUT --data-binary @$p "$BASE/remote.php/dav/uploads/$USER/$ID/$n"; n=$((n+1)); done
> # succeeds:
> curl -X MOVE -H "Destination: $BASE/remote.php/dav/files/$USER/out.pdf" -H "OC-Total-Length: 102395904" \
>      "$BASE/remote.php/dav/uploads/$USER/$ID/.file"
> # stores 0 bytes, returns 201:
> curl -X MOVE -H "Destination: $BASE/remote.php/dav/files/$USER/out.pdf" -H "OC-Total-Length: 102395904" \
>      -H "Content-Length: 0" "$BASE/remote.php/dav/uploads/$USER/$ID/.file"
> ```
> 
> **Workaround without patching PHP.** MOVE never carries a body, so the length can be blanked for that method in nginx:
> 
> ```nginx
> map $request_method $nc_content_length {
>     default $content_length;
>     MOVE    "";
> }
> ```
> 
> and inside the PHP location, *after* `include fastcgi_params;` (with duplicate FastCGI params the last one wins):
> 
> ```nginx
> fastcgi_param CONTENT_LENGTH $nc_content_length;
> fastcgi_param HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH $nc_content_length;
> ```
> 
> Both names are required because `Request::getHeader()` checks `HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH` first and only then falls back to `CONTENT_LENGTH`. Verified: all four rows above become correct, a plain 20971520-byte PUT still stores 20971520, and a genuinely empty file still stores 0 bytes.
> 
> **Possible fix** — treat a zero-length header as absent, so the stream's own size is used:
> 
> ```php
> $expected = ($lengthHeader !== '' && (int)$lengthHeader > 0) ? (int)$lengthHeader : null;
> ```
> 
> A real 0-byte PUT then takes the `fstat()` path and still writes 0 bytes, so that case is unchanged. Arguably the assembly path should not consult the request's `Content-Length` at all, since it never describes the stream being assembled.
> 
> Happy to open this as a separate issue if it's considered distinct from the chunked-encoding case reported here.
>  

 _Originally posted by @mosi-kha in [#7995](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/7995#issuecomment-5386118425)_

cases.issue_title: [Bug]: Email shares store expiration in a different timezone and omit file_target
cases.issue_body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [x] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [x] This issue is **not** already reported on GitHub or the Nextcloud Community Forum. I searched for `sharebymail expiration timezone`, `ocMailShare file_target`, `share_type 4 expiration`, and related variants.
- [x] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. This was checked against Nextcloud 33.0.3 and current `master` code.
- [x] I agree to follow Nextcloud's Code of Conduct.

### Bug description

Email shares (`share_type = 4`, provider id `ocMailShare`) do not persist share metadata consistently with user shares and public link shares:

1. The expiration date is stored with a different timezone conversion behavior.
2. `file_target` is stored as `NULL` for newly created email shares.

For the expiration date, the OCS share API parses `expireDate` in the configured/user timezone and `OC\Share20\Manager::validateExpirationDateLink()` normalizes link/email share expiration to the end of the selected day (`23:59:59`) in that timezone. Public link shares then go through `OC\Share20\DefaultShareProvider`, which clones the expiration date and converts it to `date_default_timezone_get()` before writing it to the database.

Email shares go through `OCA\ShareByMail\ShareByMailProvider::addShareToDB()` instead. That method writes the original `DateTimeInterface` directly as `expiration` and does not set `file_target`. This creates different database values for the same selected expiration date compared with public link shares.

This is easiest to see on non-UTC timezones such as `Asia/Tokyo`.

Relevant code paths in current `master`:

- `apps/files_sharing/lib/Controller/ShareAPIController.php`: `parseDate()` creates the date in `$this->dateTimeZone->getTimeZone()`.
- `lib/private/Share20/Manager.php`: `validateExpirationDateLink()` sets link/email expiration to `23:59:59` in the configured timezone.
- `lib/private/Share20/DefaultShareProvider.php`: normal providers clone expiration, convert it to `date_default_timezone_get()`, and persist `file_target`.
- `apps/sharebymail/lib/ShareByMailProvider.php`: `addShareToDB()` persists `$expirationTime` directly and does not write `file_target`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Nextcloud instance with PHP/Nextcloud timezone set to a non-UTC timezone, for example `Asia/Tokyo`.
2. Enable `files_sharing` and `sharebymail`.
3. Create a folder, for example `/Documents`.
4. Create a public link share for `/Documents` with an expiration date, for example `2026-05-19`.
5. Create an email share for the same `/Documents` folder with the same expiration date, for example to `recipient@example.invalid`.
6. Compare the generated rows in `oc_share`, especially `share_type`, `expiration`, and `file_target`.

Example query:

```sql
SELECT id, share_type, share_with, file_source, file_target, expiration
FROM oc_share
WHERE file_source = <fileid>
ORDER BY id;
```

### Expected behavior

Email shares should persist the selected expiration date consistently with public link shares.

For a selected expiration date in a non-UTC timezone, `share_type = 4` should resolve to the same effective end-of-day instant as `share_type = 3`.

Email shares should also persist `file_target` for the shared file/folder path, the same way the default share provider does for user and public link shares.

### Nextcloud Server version

33

### Operating system

Other

### PHP engine version

PHP 8.2

### Web server

Nginx

### Database engine version

MariaDB

### Is this bug present after an update or on a fresh install?

Fresh Nextcloud Server install

### Are you using the Nextcloud Server Encryption module?

Encryption is Disabled

### What user-backends are you using?

- [x] Default user-backend _(database)_
- [ ] LDAP/ Active Directory
- [ ] SSO - SAML
- [ ] Other

### Configuration report

```json
{
    "dbtype": "mysql",
    "version": "33.0.3.3",
    "default_timezone": "Asia/Tokyo"
}
```

### List of activated Apps

```shell
- files_sharing
- sharebymail
```

### Nextcloud Signing status

```shell
No errors have been found.
```

### Nextcloud Logs

```json
No relevant server log entry is generated. The issue is visible in the persisted oc_share row.
```

### Additional info

This appears related to the provider-specific create/update path for email shares rather than to a database engine issue.

`ShareByMailProvider::addShareToDB()` currently does not mirror the normalization used by `DefaultShareProvider` before writing `expiration`, and it does not write `file_target` at all.

PR #58128 changed share expiration to end-of-day (`23:59:59`). This report is not about that behavior change itself; it is about email shares not persisting the same effective expiration instant as public link shares after that normalization.

cases.issue_body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [x] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [x] This issue is **not** already reported on [Github](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) OR [Nextcloud Community Forum](https://help.nextcloud.com/) _(I've searched it)_.
- [x] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. See [Maintenance and Release Schedule](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/wiki/Maintenance-and-Release-Schedule) for supported versions.
- [x] I agree to follow Nextcloud's [Code of Conduct](https://nextcloud.com/contribute/code-of-conduct/).

### Bug description

`PROPFIND` against the legacy WebDAV endpoint `/remote.php/webdav/<anything>` returns
`207 Multi-Status` for **every** path, including paths that do not exist. It should return
`404 Not Found`. The modern endpoint `/remote.php/dav/files/<uid>/...` is unaffected and
still returns `404`.

This breaks Windows mapped network drives. Explorer's "New Folder" flow probes for a free
name with `PROPFIND` and only sends `MKCOL` once it gets a `404`. Since the legacy endpoint
never answers `404`, Explorer concludes every candidate name is taken, never sends `MKCOL`,
and throws its own "Access denied" dialog. No `403` is ever returned, and — this is the fun
part — **nothing whatsoever is written to `nextcloud.log`**, because `ExceptionLoggerPlugin`
classifies `NotFound` as non-fatal. So from the server's point of view the request is a
complete success, and from the user's point of view the share is broken. Enjoy explaining
that one to your users.

I lost most of a day to this before giving up on the "obviously it's a permissions problem"
theory and reading the diff. Root cause, for whoever gets to fix it:

**`Server::$streamMultiStatus = true;`** in
[`apps/dav/lib/Connector/Sabre/ServerFactory.php:83`](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/master/apps/dav/lib/Connector/Sabre/ServerFactory.php#L83).

Introduced by commit `ab34c4c21884` *"perf(dav): Stream PROPFIND output"*, backported to
stable33 as **#62225**, first shipped in **33.0.7**. It is the only occurrence of that flag
in the entire tree, and it is set unconditionally.

The chain (sabre/dav 4.7.0, as vendored):

1. `CorePlugin::httpPropFind()` line 327 calls `Server::getPropertiesIteratorForPath()`.
   That method contains `yield`, so it is a **generator** — calling it executes none of its
   body. The `$this->tree->getNodeForPath($path)` inside it (`Server.php:971`) never runs at
   this point.
2. Line 330, immediately after: `$response->setStatus(207)`. Unconditionally, with nothing
   resolved and nothing validated.
3. Line 346: `generateMultiStatus()`. With streaming enabled (`Server.php:1641-1646`) this
   returns a **closure** rather than a serialized body. Still nothing iterated.
4. `Server::invokeMethod()` line 490 → `Sapi::sendResponse()` line 64 flushes the **207
   status line and headers**, then line 81 invokes the closure.
5. *Now* the generator finally runs, `ObjectTree::getNodeForPath()` throws
   `Sabre\DAV\Exception\NotFound` as it always has, and the catch block in
   `OCA\DAV\Connector\Sabre\Server::start()` dutifully sets the status to 404 and re-sends —
   into a response whose headers left the building one stack frame ago.

So the 404 logic is fine. It just runs after the status code has already been committed to
the wire. The body that comes back is a degenerate multistatus: `writeMultiStatus()` gets as
far as the XML prolog and the opening `<d:multistatus>`, then the first loop iteration
throws, `$w->flush()` never runs, and the `d:error` document from the exception handler is
appended on top. That is why the responses are a uniform ~1150–1350 bytes regardless of
which non-existent path you ask for.

**Affected endpoints** — everything routed through `ServerFactory`:

| Endpoint | Entry point | Affected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/remote.php/webdav` | `apps/dav/appinfo/v1/webdav.php` | ❌ yes |
| `/remote.php/files` | same file (`remote.php:87`) | ❌ yes |
| `/public.php/webdav` | `apps/dav/appinfo/v1/publicwebdav.php` | ❌ yes |
| `/public.php/dav` | `apps/dav/appinfo/v2/publicremote.php` | ❌ yes |
| `/remote.php/dav` | `apps/dav/appinfo/v2/remote.php` → `OCA\DAV\Server` | ✅ no |

`/remote.php/dav` never touches the flag, which is exactly why the modern endpoint still
behaves. That asymmetry is the whole tell.

I also checked whether any plugin on the legacy server happens to resolve the node during
`beforeMethod:PROPFIND` and would incidentally save us. None does: `LockPlugin` returns
early unless the method is `PUT`, `ViewOnlyPlugin` only hooks `GET`/`COPY`/`MOVE`, and
`FilesPlugin` hooks `propFind`, which fires *inside* the generator and is therefore also too
late. Nothing catches this.

**Version status:**

| Version | `streamMultiStatus` present |
| --- | --- |
| 32.0.13 | no |
| 33.0.5 | no |
| 33.0.6 | no |
| 33.0.7 | **yes** ← regression enters |
| 34.0.3 | **yes** |
| `master`, `stable33`, `stable34` (checked at time of writing) | **yes** |

Reproduced live on 33.0.7.1. I then pulled the 34.0.3 release tarball and audited it
line-by-line specifically to find out whether upgrading would save me. It would not.


### Steps to reproduce

You need an app password — SAML/SSO accounts can't do basic auth against WebDAV.

1. Create an app password for a test account (Settings → Security → Devices & sessions).
2. `PROPFIND` a path that definitively does not exist, on both endpoints:

```bash
NCUSER='testuser'
NCPASS='xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx'
HOST='https://cloud.example.com'
MISSING="__nonexistent_$(date +%s)__"

# legacy endpoint  -> returns 207, should be 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'legacy: %{http_code}\n' -u "$NCUSER:$NCPASS" \
     -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 0' "$HOST/remote.php/webdav/$MISSING"

# modern endpoint  -> correctly returns 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'modern: %{http_code}\n' -u "$NCUSER:$NCPASS" \
     -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 0' "$HOST/remote.php/dav/files/$NCUSER/$MISSING"
```

Observed:

```
legacy: 207
modern: 404
```

3. Inspect the legacy body and note that it is not a real multistatus:

```bash
curl -s -u "$NCUSER:$NCPASS" -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 0' \
     "$HOST/remote.php/webdav/$MISSING" | head -c 400
```

4. Optional, the way real users hit it: map a network drive in Windows Explorer to
   `https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/webdav`, then right-click → New → Folder.
   The folder is never created; Explorer shows "Access denied". The access log shows a burst
   of `PROPFIND … 207` for `Neuer Ordner` / `New folder` and `desktop.ini`, and **no**
   `MKCOL` is ever sent, because Explorer is still waiting for a `404` that will never come:

```
203.0.113.10 [.../...] "PROPFIND /remote.php/webdav/Foo/Bar"                  207 1334
203.0.113.10 [.../...] "PROPFIND /remote.php/webdav/Foo/Bar/Neuer%20Ordner"   207 1155   <- should be 404
203.0.113.10 [.../...] "PROPFIND /remote.php/webdav/Foo/Bar/desktop.ini"      207 1154   <- should be 404
```

For comparison, the same operation against `/remote.php/dav/files/<uid>/` on the same server,
same minute, working exactly as intended:

```
198.51.100.20 [.../...] "PROPFIND .../Foo/Neuer%20Ordner"   404
198.51.100.20 [.../...] "MKCOL    .../Foo/Neuer%20Ordner"   201
198.51.100.20 [.../...] "PROPPATCH .../Foo/Neuer%20Ordner"  207
198.51.100.20 [.../...] "MOVE     .../Foo/Neuer%20Ordner"   201
```

5. If you want the aggregate version: grep your access log for
   `"PROPFIND /remote.php/webdav`. On 33.0.6 you get a steady stream of `404`s every single
   day. From the moment 33.0.7 is installed you get **exactly zero**, forever. In my case
   that was ~265 000 legacy PROPFINDs across twelve days without a single `404`. The cutover
   is visible to the second in the log, matched against the updater timestamp.


### Expected behavior

`PROPFIND` on a non-existent path returns `404 Not Found` on the legacy endpoint, the same
way it does on `/remote.php/dav` and the same way it did in 33.0.6 and every release before
it. `207 Multi-Status` should mean the resource exists and here are its properties, not
"I already sent the headers, sorry".

Concretely: the node must be resolved *before* the status code is committed. The streaming
optimisation is fine in principle, it just needs to prime the generator first. Priming with
a single `->current()` on the iterator before `setStatus(207)` runs the generator up to its
first `yield`, which triggers `getNodeForPath()` and lets `NotFound` propagate while the
status is still mutable — and a subsequent `foreach` still works, since the generator has not
advanced past the first yield. That preserves the perf win for the normal case.

Failing that: make the flag opt-in via a config value, or revert the line on the stable
branches until it can be done safely. Silently converting every 404 into a 207 on an endpoint
that Windows depends on is not a great trade for saving some memory on PROPFIND.

cases.issue_title: Client session note removals are not persisted with persistent user sessions
cases.issue_body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

core

### Describe the bug

With persistent user sessions (default since 25.0.0), writing an authenticated client session note is persisted, but removing 
one is silently dropped. `AuthenticatedClientSessionModel#removeNote` and `restartClientSession()` (which clears all notes) 
only update the cached entity; the database keeps the note for the lifetime of the session, and it resurfaces whenever the 
session is re-read from the database (restart, failover, cache eviction). 

Root cause: `JpaChangesPerformer#mergeClientSession` replays the recorded update tasks against a synthetic `AuthenticatedClientSessionEntity` whose `getNotes()` returns a fresh anonymous `HashMap` that only overrides get and put. 
remove, clear, containsKey, iteration etc. run against that throwaway map, so `removeNote` -> `entity.getNotes().remove(name)` 
and `restartClientSession()` -> `entity.getNotes().clear()` never reach the persisted model. 
The user session counterpart in `mergeUserSession` does override remove/clear, so this looks like an oversight rather than intended. 

### Version

26.7.2

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Removed and cleared client session notes are absent from the persisted client session after the transaction commits.

### Actual behavior

Every note ever written stays in the persisted row; only overwrites (put) are persisted.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create a user session and a client session, set a note on the client session.  
2. In a new transaction, call clientSession.removeNote(name) (or restartClientSession()).  
3. Read the client session back via UserSessionPersisterProvider#loadClientSession (or SELECT data FROM offline_client_session): the note is still there.

### Anything else?

Observed with 26.7.2 but seems to be like this since 25.0.0.

`26.0.0` and `26.6.4`:

```java
// services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/RoleMapperResource.java
return realm.getRolesStream()
        .filter(roleMapper::hasRole)
        .map(toBriefRepresentation);
```

It iterates over **every role defined in the realm** — not the roles the principal
actually holds — and evaluates `hasRole()` against each one.

### Why this is especially expensive for group-derived roles

For a `UserModel`, `hasRole()` evaluates two independent paths:

```java
// model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/UserAdapter.java
public boolean hasRole(RoleModel role) {
    return RoleUtils.hasRole(getRoleMappingsStream(), role)
        || RoleUtils.hasRoleFromGroup(getGroupsStream(), role, true);
}
```

and each containment check re-expands the composite graph from scratch:

```java
// model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/RoleAdapter.java
public boolean hasRole(RoleModel role) {
    return this.equals(role) || KeycloakModelUtils.searchFor(role, this, new HashSet<>());
}
```

`searchFor()` allocates a **fresh `HashSet` on every invocation** — there is no
memoization across the outer loop.

In deployments where users receive roles through **group membership** (a very common
pattern), the first path returns `false` only *after* fully expanding the user's direct
mappings, and only then does the second path run and walk every group plus its parent
chain. Both paths execute for every realm role, which makes the group-based model the
worst case rather than an edge case.

Effective complexity: **O(C × M × D)**, where C is the total number of realm roles, M the
number of role mappings reachable from the principal, and D the composite expansion depth.

### The fix already exists in the codebase

`ClientRoleMappingsResource.getCompositeClientRoleMappings()` was changed in 26.6.4 to
compute the effective set once and then filter:

```java
// 26.6.4
return RoleUtils.getDeepRoleMappings(user).stream()
        .filter(r -> r.isClientRole() && r.getContainerId().equals(client.getId()))
        .map(toBriefRepresentation);
```

`RoleUtils.getDeepRoleMappings()` was added in 26.6.4 (`server-spi`) and already handles
group inheritance including the parent chain:

```java
public static Set<RoleModel> getDeepUserRoleMappings(UserModel user) {
    Set<RoleModel> roleMappings = user.getRoleMappingsStream().collect(Collectors.toSet());
    user.getGroupsStream().forEach(group -> addGroupRoles(group, roleMappings));
    return expandCompositeRoles(roleMappings);
}

private static void addGroupRoles(GroupModel group, Set<RoleModel> roleMappings) {
    roleMappings.addAll(group.getRoleMappingsStream().collect(Collectors.toSet()));
    if (group.getParentId() == null) return;
    addGroupRoles(group.getParent(), roleMappings);
}
```

The helper needed to fix the realm endpoint is therefore already present and already
exercised in production by the client endpoint — it simply was not wired up here.

---


### Version

Reproduced on both 26.0.0 and 26.6.4 — identical behaviour, no improvement after upgrading.  This matches source inspection: RoleMapperResource.getCompositeRealmRoleMappings() is byte-for-byte identical across tags 26.0.0 and 26.6.4, while the equivalent client endpoint was rewritten in 26.6.4 as part of #47157.

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

`GET /users/{user-id}/role-mappings/realm/composite` should resolve the principal's
effective realm roles in time proportional to the size of that principal's own effective
role set, not to the total number of roles defined in the realm — matching the behaviour
of the client endpoint after the #47157 fix.

Retrieving the full set of roles a user holds, whether assigned directly or inherited
through groups, parent groups, or composite roles, is a legitimate and common
administrative need. Today this endpoint is the only API that answers that question, and
at realm scale it is not usable.

If maintainers prefer to leave the current endpoint's semantics untouched, an equally
acceptable resolution would be a dedicated endpoint that returns a principal's effective
roles computed via `RoleUtils.getDeepRoleMappings()`.

---

### Actual behavior

Response time scales with the total number of realm roles, independent of how many roles
the user actually holds. The work is CPU-bound and allocates a large number of
short-lived `HashSet` instances.

### Measured environment

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Realm roles in realm (C) | **7,976** |
| Effective realm roles for the test user (Y) | **5,862** |
| How the user obtains them | **entirely through group membership** — no direct user→role mappings |
| Approximate containment checks per request | ~7,976 × ~5,862 ≈ **46.7 million** |

### Endpoint vs. equivalent SQL

| | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `GET …/users/{id}/role-mappings/realm/composite` — **26.0.0** | **7.92 s** | 5,862 roles · 1.19 MB |
| `GET …/users/{id}/role-mappings/realm/composite` — **26.6.4** | **unchanged** | 5,862 roles · 1.19 MB |
| Equivalent recursive CTE against the same database | **0.058 s** | 5,862 rows |
| **Ratio** | **≈ 136×** | identical result set |

Both return the **same 5,862 roles**. The database is not the bottleneck; the entire cost
sits in the per-role `hasRole()` loop in the resource layer.

Upgrading from 26.0.0 to 26.6.4 produced **no measurable improvement** on this endpoint,
which is expected given that the resource method was not part of the #47157 change.

### Roles model fine-grained API permissions

The realm defines one role per API operation, which is what drives C into the thousands.
Anonymised examples of the naming pattern:

```
svc_alpha_test_get_entity_list_odata
svc_alpha_test_put_entity_status_update
svc_beta_v2_test_get_public_city_odata
svc_gamma_test_post_project_member
```

Roles are attached to groups and users are made members of those groups. Roles and groups
grow continuously as new services and resources are onboarded, so C only increases over
time.

---

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create a realm and define a large number of realm roles — e.g. **8,000**, named to
   mimic per-operation permissions.
2. Make a subset of them composite so that expansion has depth (for example a few hundred
   composites, each bundling 10–20 leaf roles).
3. Create a group hierarchy and attach the roles to **groups**, not directly to users, so
   the group-inheritance path in `UserAdapter.hasRole()` is exercised.
4. Create a user and add them to groups such that their effective realm role set is large.
   In the environment measured above this resolves to **5,862** roles.
5. Call the endpoint and measure wall-clock time:

   ```
   GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}/role-mappings/realm/composite
   ```

6. Run the equivalent query directly against the database and compare:

   ```sql
   WITH RECURSIVE direct_roles AS (
       -- roles inherited through group membership
       SELECT grm.role_id
       FROM public.user_group_membership ugm
       JOIN public.group_role_mapping grm ON grm.group_id = ugm.group_id
       WHERE ugm.user_id = '<user-id>'
       UNION
       -- roles assigned directly to the user
       SELECT urm.role_id
       FROM public.user_role_mapping urm
       WHERE urm.user_id = '<user-id>'
   ),
   all_roles AS (
       SELECT role_id FROM direct_roles
       UNION
       SELECT cr.child_role
       FROM public.composite_role cr
       JOIN all_roles t ON t.role_id = cr.composite
   )
   SELECT kr.id, kr."name"
   FROM all_roles t
   JOIN public.keycloak_role kr ON kr.id = t.role_id
   WHERE kr.client_role = false
   ORDER BY 2;
   ```

   In the environment above this returns the **same 5,862 roles in 0.058 s**, versus
   **7.92 s** for the endpoint.

7. Repeat step 5 on 26.6.4. The timing is unchanged.

8. For contrast, run the same test against
   `GET /users/{user-id}/role-mappings/clients/{client-id}/composite` with a comparable
   number of client roles — on 26.6.4 that endpoint no longer degrades.

---

### Anything else?

### Proposed fix

Apply the same pattern used for the client endpoint. `RoleUtils` already exposes an
`isRealmRole(RoleModel, RealmModel)` overload, which is a safer filter than negating
`isClientRole()`:

```java
// RoleMapperResource.getCompositeRealmRoleMappings()
return RoleUtils.getDeepRoleMappings(roleMapper).stream()
        .filter(r -> RoleUtils.isRealmRole(r, realm))
        .map(toBriefRepresentation);
```

`RoleMapperResource` serves both users and groups. `getDeepRoleMappings()` already
branches on `UserModel` vs `GroupModel`, so both callers remain correct.

### Note on ordering

The current implementation emits roles in `realm.getRolesStream()` order, whereas a
`Set`-based implementation does not guarantee an order. The client endpoint already
accepted this trade-off in 26.6.4. If deterministic ordering is desired, sorting by name
before mapping would preserve it at negligible cost.

### Related code

- #47157 — same root cause, fixed for the client endpoint in 26.6.4
- `services/.../admin/RoleMapperResource.java` → `getCompositeRealmRoleMappings()` (unchanged)
- `services/.../admin/ClientRoleMappingsResource.java` → `getCompositeClientRoleMappings()` (fixed)
- `server-spi/.../models/utils/RoleUtils.java` → `getDeepRoleMappings()` (added 26.6.4)
- `model/jpa/.../UserAdapter.java` → `hasRole()`
- `model/jpa/.../RoleAdapter.java` → `hasRole()` → `KeycloakModelUtils.searchFor(..., new HashSet<>())`

### Current workaround

We currently resolve effective roles with the recursive SQL query above. It is correct and
fast, but it bypasses the Admin API, couples our services to the internal database schema,
and will break on any schema change. We would much rather use the supported API.
---

cases.issue_title: Usage of second class configuration may not be masked in show-config
cases.issue_body:
It's documented that you shouldn't use second-class options, such as KC_SPI_VAULT__KEYSTORE__PASS and you should see a warning about using a "second-class" option, but if one it can appear unmasked in show-config.

There's two related cases:

1. Usage of even the proper second class key in the env, e.g. KC_SPI_FOO__BAR__KEY, is turned into `kc.spi-foo--bar--key` by the KcEnvConfigSource, but the EnvConfigSource assumes that it's kc.spi.foo."bar".key - which is then shown in show-config

2. The legacy key format kc.spi-foo-bar-key in any config source.

I don't think we looked at using the FallbackConfigSourceInterceptor for the second case - it's just being handled in the MicroProfileConfigProvider.

_Originally posted by @shawkins in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/51013#discussion_r3626265935_
